description: List the organization's monitor and heartbeat incidents, newest first, to see what is or was down and which alerts went out. Each item has id, monitor_id or heartbeat_id (exactly one is set), started_at, resolved_at (null while open), cause, cause_detail (the raw check error), acknowledged_at and notification_logs: the alerts sent, oldest first, each with id, channel_type (EMAIL, TELEGRAM, WEBHOOK, SLACK or DISCORD), destination (may be masked), event (TRIGGERED for the first alert and every reminder, RESOLVED for the recovery), sent_at, status (PENDING while a webhook, Slack or Discord delivery is still being tried, then SENT or FAILED) and error (the last delivery error). For one incident's full record use get_incident; for the checks behind it use list_check_results; incidents posted on a status page are list_status_page_incidents. An incident resolves by itself when its monitor or heartbeat recovers. Returns a page: items plus total, page, size and pages. An invalid value is a 422 naming the argument. Example: {"status": "open", "size": 50}

cause.description: Keep one failure cause, such as TIMEOUT, HTTP_5XX or HEARTBEAT_MISSED.

monitor_id.description: Keep one monitor's incidents: its uuid from list_monitors.

period_days.description: Keep incidents active within the last N days, 1 to 365. An open incident always qualifies, so with status open it changes nothing: use status resolved, or omit status, to see the window take effect.

size.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100; default 25. Keep paging until you have seen total rows.

status.description: open or resolved (lowercase); omit it for both.

name: list_incidents

cause.description: Known values: TIMEOUT, DNS_FAILURE, CONNECTION_REFUSED, TLS_INVALID, HTTP_4XX, HTTP_5XX, HTTP_UNEXPECTED_STATUS, KEYWORD_MISSING, TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS, TARGET_BLOCKED, PORT_STATE_MISMATCH, INVALID_TARGET, HEARTBEAT_MISSED, HEARTBEAT_FAILED, UNKNOWN.

channel_type.description: Known values: EMAIL, TELEGRAM, WEBHOOK, SLACK, DISCORD.

title: List incidents
